title: deployment-compatibility-adapter-multimode-inference
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: customers expect identical semantics for canary rollouts, A/B tests, shadow traffic, and automatic rollback across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. In practice config parity breaks due to environment-specific constraints: private VPC egress rules, KMS/HSM integration latency, constrained GPU pool shapes in Dedicated, and differing admission controllers. These break existing rollout policies and cause silent failures or unsafe exposure during canaries.

Goal: build a Deployment Compatibility Adapter (DCA) that translates a canonical rollout spec into environment-safe plans, enforces preflight validation, simulates resource constraints, and provides deterministic rollback triggers that work across all modes. The adapter must be lightweight, verifiable, and integrable with the existing rollout orchestrator.

Scope: translation layer + validation + simulation harness + telemetry contract for canary/AB/shadow flows. Not in scope: changing tenant billing or core runtime kernels.

Constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Strict parity vs safe subset: we prefer a conservative, environment-aware subset of rollout constructs for Private (no cross-tenant shadowing without explicit networking permission).
- Latency-sensitive metrics: Private with KMS-backed key unwrap adds headroom; we will weight rollouts to avoid triggering p95 alarms.
- Resource-aware fractions: Dedicated clusters have fixed GPU pools; large canary fractions cause OOM risk so we simulate capacity before applying.
- Developer ergonomics vs explicit controls: provide sane defaults and an escape hatch via explicit flags for advanced customers.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter accepts canonical rollout spec and emits environment-specific plan for Hosted, Dedicated, Private
Preflight simulator detects capacity and network constraints and blocks unsafe rollouts
Telemetry emitted for canary fraction, observed p50/p95, error budget impact, and shadow cost estimate
Auto-rollback triggers are consistent across modes and validated end-to-end in staging
Documentation and example configs for customers and SEs included in Console and PRD
implementation_notes: Create a canonical rollout schema extension that includes environment hints (eg. max_fraction_per_tier, allowed_shadowing)
Adapter to implement translation rules for three environment families: hosted, dedicated, private
Preflight simulator to reuse existing load-harness (ENG-33177) to run 30s synthetic burst tests and capacity checks
Integrate with Console to surface recommended safe fraction and blocked reasons
Expose a dry-run API endpoint that returns a delta plan and risk score
Auto-rollback will use fused metrics: latency regressions (p95 increase > 30%), error rate (>0.5% absolute), and eval-set quality drop (>5%)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly conservative translations could degrade customer rollout capabilities. Mitigation: provide opt-in advanced mode with explicit customer sign-off.
Risk: Simulator false negatives (misses a Dedicated OOM). Mitigation: run multi-configuration simulations and require capacity reserve guarantees for Dedicated commits.
Risk: Private deployments with air-gapped KGMs may block telemetry. Mitigation: fail closed for safety; provide on-prem telemetry adapters and local dashboard artifacts.
Risk: Increased rollout latency due to additional validations. Mitigation: make validation parallel and cache environment capabilities; tune to sub-second planning where possible.
